standard_prerequisites.name: Pushforward of a K-injective complex along an open immersion is K-injective
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma lemma-K-injective-flat (tag 0D5Z)
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies computing R-H_Z(Rj_*K) from the complex j_*I^bullet, and hence the reduction to abelian sheaves.

core_obligations: Choose a K-injective complex I^bullet representing K and note that j_*I^bullet represents Rj_*K and is again K-injective, so H_Z(j_*I^bullet) represents R-H_Z(Rj_*K) (proof lines 8696-8700).
Reduce to abelian sheaves: show H_Z(j_*G) = 0 for any abelian sheaf G on U, i.e. that a section s of j_*G over W supported on W cap Z vanishes (proof lines 8701-8704).
Use the support condition s|(W minus W cap Z) = 0 together with the identity j_*G(W) = G(U cap W) = j_*G(W minus W cap Z) to conclude s = 0 (proof lines 8704-8707).
proof_roadmap: Replace K by a K-injective representative and record that its pushforward stays K-injective.
Reduce the vanishing to a statement about abelian sheaves with support.
Compare sections on W and on W minus the closed subset to force the section to vanish.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows R-H_Z(Rj_*K) = 0 whenever j : U -> X is the inclusion of an open subset disjoint from the closed subset Z. The proof replaces K by a K-injective representative I^bullet, uses that j_*I^bullet is again K-injective so that H_Z(j_*I^bullet) computes R-H_Z(Rj_*K), and then reduces to the level of abelian sheaves: a section of j_*G over W supported on W cap Z must vanish, because W minus W cap Z meets the same sections as W does for a pushforward along j (proof lines 8696-8707). H2: the reduction to K-injective representatives and the support computation on the level of abelian sheaves are the substance.
